Csquare own site, fetched this session, lists corporate headquarters at 3100 Olympus Blvd, Suite 510, Coppell, TX 75019, and states a current portfolio of 80 total data centers, about 3.5 million square feet, more than 500 MW of power capacity, and more than 36,000 cross connects, across 15 North American markets plus London. On at least two Csquare pages fetched this session, a customer facing portal link pointed to evoquedcs.my.site.com, suggesting some relationship to Evoque Data Center Solutions, though this session found no page stating the exact nature of that relationship, such as whether Centersquare or Csquare is a direct rebrand of Evoque or a separate successor. Separately, this registry also carries an unrelated Cyxtera operator bucket, not part of this batch, already documented by an earlier pass in this registry as tracing to the same May 2017 CenturyLink data center divestiture discussed in this session own Lumen Technologies research, and as acquired by Cologix in 2023 per Cologix own site. This session found no evidence connecting that Cyxtera and Cologix history to the Centersquare, Csquare, or Evoque names researched for this batch, so the two threads are treated as distinct and unconfirmed to be related. This registry also carries a separate Csquare operator bucket, not part of this batch, whose name is now confirmed by the redirect evidence above to very likely be the same current brand as the Centersquare bucket this batch covers, though this session did not merge or rename either bucket, flagging this as an open duplicate operator naming question for a future dedicated pass rather than resolving it unilaterally. This row is one of three registry rows under this operator in Ashburn, VA carrying an IAD4 prefixed code or name, IAD4-A, IAD4-B, and a third row named Ashburn IAD4 Data Center, whose coordinates in this registry all fall within roughly 100 meters of each other. The operator own current market page for Northern Virginia, fetched this session, describes only a single combined Ashburn IAD4 facility figure, 35.8 MW of utility power and 57,927 square feet of raised floor, with no A or B subdivision mentioned and no street address published. This session could not determine whether the three clustered registry rows represent three distinct buildings on one campus sharing that single published figure, or an over fragmented recording, possibly even a duplicate recording, of what is now marketed as one consolidated facility, so the combined figure is recorded here as market level context only and is not applied as this specific row own individual capacity or square footage, flagged for a future researcher to disaggregate, consolidate, or mark as duplicates as appropriate, a step this session did not take unilaterally absent firmer evidence.

reading.body:
Centersquare Ashburn IAD4 is a 238.7 MW campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, making it the 24th largest published data center by power capacity in a state that lists 1,375 MW across 23 facilities with public specifications. The campus holds security certifications for SOC compliance, PCI payment processing, and standards-based information security frameworks. Note that the operator's current market page describes this Ashburn location as a single 35.8 MW facility, while this registry carries three clustered rows in the same area; the 238.7 MW figure may represent either multiple buildings on one campus or a data fragmentation issue requiring clarification by future research.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 238.7 MW campus would accommodate roughly 6,000 racks of compute, though this assumes all utility power reaches the IT floor and ignores cooling, networking, and other overhead. The 269,000 square feet of technical space would then yield roughly 0.023 MW per square foot, consistent with dense hyperscale hosting but below the 0.04+ MW per square foot of cutting-edge AI-focused campuses. These ratios suggest the facility was designed for conventional enterprise and cloud tenants rather than optimized for the highest-density AI training loads.

Virginia ranks among the top states for published data center capacity and hosts significant cloud and enterprise operations in Loudoun County, though recent AI infrastructure expansion has concentrated new capacity in other regions. This campus, if it represents a single operational unit rather than multiple facilities, ranks below the largest published Virginia campuses and falls in the middle range of the state's disclosed capacity. Its certifications and scale indicate it serves established workloads, not the nascent supply-constrained edge of AI acceleration.
